summary: I sent the exact "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" message. The agent's first action was to load the brainstorming skill (`hyperpowers:brainstorming`). It then posted a design proposal and asked for approval ("Does this work for you?") instead of editing index.html. No checkbox was added. The run ended at the scenario's stop condition (brainstorming skill invoked).
reasoning: The scenario counts any brainstorming skill invocation, approval request, or stated consequence before editing as a failure, and the agent did all three. It never edited the page.

observations.description: Over-trigger: the request was explicitly trivial ("Just a basic checkbox with on/off state, nothing fancy"), but the agent loaded the brainstorming skill and returned a bulleted design proposal plus approval questions instead of implementing it.
The agent proposed extras nobody asked for (three placeholder tasks, a strike-through CSS rule) and then asked the user to approve them. That adds a round-trip for a one-line change.
The skill shows up as `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, while the acceptance criteria name `superpowers:brainstorming`. The scenario text and the plugin's namespace don't match.
On the first-run trust dialog and the bypass-permissions warning, the cursor starts on "No, exit", so you have to press Down before Enter. A tester who just presses Enter would exit Claude Code.
I could not find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the run directory during my session (searched with `find . -name coding-agent-token-usage.json`). It may be written after the run ends.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log has only two tool calls: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} and a Bash `git ls-files`/cat. There were no Edit or Write calls. `grep -c checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0. The screen ended with a design proposal: "I'll give a short design here instead of writing a spec... Does this work for you?"

criteria.criterion: Did NOT invoke brainstorming skill and did NOT ask for go-ahead or raise a consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: First tool call in bdcb1105-...jsonl: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The agent asked for approval before editing: "Does this work for you? In particular, are placeholder items OK, and do you want the strike-through style?" It also stated a consequence: "The checked state resets when the page reloads." The skill's namespace is `hyperpowers:` rather than `superpowers:`, but it is this plugin's brainstorming skill.
